scope: Great Eastern Main Line / Old Lea / Channelsea / Bromley-by-Bow gasworks inclusive; western Old Lea industrial frontage from Three Mills to the railway; reviewed industrial roofs between Channelsea and the Woolwich railway
method: Individual building/range envelopes manually read from period maps. Dimensions and elevations are reconstruction estimates; each record separates mapped floor marks from selected model heights.

author-os-footprints-1891-96.method: Reviewed one-to-one geometry corrections. Complex compounds and architectural landmarks require separate review; source feature IDs retained. Source boundary simplification tolerance 0.05 m. Explicitly reviewed groups; OS external boundaries with retained Goad compartments, uses and elevations. Millimetre coordinate rounding only. Explicit reviewed Imperial mill and separate Towers courtyard groups; OS outer boundaries retain Goad compartments and elevation evidence. Millimetre rounding only. Explicit OS/Goad-reviewed Oil Wharf ranges, four petroleum tanks and one disused tank; open storage cleared of spurious models. Explicit local OS/Goad matches across Howards; interpreted internal Goad compartments within surveyed outer boundaries. Explicit OS/Goad cooperage and Winstone groups; retained elevation evidence and interpreted internal compartments. Explicit reviewed OS/Goad matches west of the cooperage, retaining interpreted elevations and internal compartments. Reviewed Crystal Wharf, Barber and southern ink-works exterior matches; remove open-yard misinterpretations and retain separate map/elevation evidence. Reviewed starch, tin-box and confectionery exterior groups; retained Goad uses/compartments and interpreted elevations, with explicit neighbouring Bow Bridge boundary transfers. Explicit Bow Bridge OS/Goad matches plus separately recorded direct OS trace for the missing continuous works body; interpreted room divisions and elevations retained. Explicit Hunt soap-works OS/Goad matches, with earlier room divisions and elevation interpretations retained. Explicit Lascelles and British Ultramarine OS/Goad matches; narrow OS sheet-join corrections separately recorded; prior heights and roof interpretations retained. Explicit Williams/French Asphalte OS/Goad matches; separate direct traces for missing eastern rooms; OS sheet-edge completion recorded separately; existing elevations retained. Explicit refinery/printing/machinery-depot OS/Goad matches; one direct OS storage-shed trace; five omitted rooms restored; existing elevations retained. Explicit Kendrick north/south and Usher OS/Goad matches; two sheet-seam completions, one direct L-shaped trace and two restored rooms. Existing elevations retained. Explicit northern Three Mills OS/Goad matches, one direct OS trace, one provisional local Goad transfer, mapped chimney and two tank outlines; prior elevations retained. Explicit southern Three Mills OS/Goad matches for eight existing ranges and three tank outlines; prior elevations retained. Explicit House/Clock Mill and wharf OS/Goad matches; mapped millrace relationships retained, landmark details attached to corrected footprints. Reviewed Ratner OS matches: complete courtyard exterior split into interpreted existing roof compartments; separate eastern room. Existing elevations retained. Explicit OS exteriors for Albion; separate northern/southern bodies preserve the open courtyard. Southwest disused-soap-yard envelope rejected after raw map review. Reviewed complete OS exteriors; mill north tip retains lower boiler interpretation. Explicit shared source seam reconciliation, uncertain western use and ancillary omissions recorded. Explicit rubber/oilskin and felt OS exterior matches. Manufacturing court and felt recesses remain open; northwest source division retained. Domestic industrial misclassifications rejected after raw OS review. Reviewed complete OS exteriors, retaining Goad F2 uses and relative internal compartments with prior elevations and roof parameters. Separate open courts, two enclosed manure/tallow openings and mapped chimney openings retained. Explicit OS-reviewed complete wharf exteriors and compartments; inherited height/roof interpretations; one recorded foundry source overlap. Four separate shaded OS room exteriors replace broad overlapping envelopes. Two existing kiln bodies follow circular source envelopes; elevations and roof profiles remain interpreted. Reviewed complete mill and southern Augustus Smith OS exteriors with Goad F3 room identities; one corrected misplaced mill-room identity, an interpreted coppers/stoves cut, two independently mapped chimney bases, and all prior elevations/roof parameters retained. Explicit raw-OS reviewed brewery roof exteriors; seven existing profiles retained, pale central court open, public-house frontage excluded, inferred chimney transferred with full plinth containment. Three existing profiles relocated onto explicitly reviewed shaded factory ranges; church and open western court excluded. Explicit Jeffrey glue-works complete OS exteriors reviewed against original Goad F3; inherited compartment proportions divide two compound bodies, two independently mapped square chimney bases, all previous elevations and roofs retained. Explicit reviewed chemical-works exteriors, two retained interpreted roof divisions, and independently mapped square chimney plinth; existing source-linked west/east ranges and all prior elevations/roof parameters retained. Explicit OS/Goad matches, direct trace of missing western ropewalk, removal of an unsupported open-yard envelope. Explicit process-room identity review, complete OS exterior coverage with interpreted Goad compartment cuts, eleven retained ranges and one independently mapped round 200-foot chimney. Prior elevations and roof profiles retained. Nine retained ranges matched explicitly to OS exteriors; missing southern roof traced with supplied terminal walls. Goad alterations and approximate compartment identities recorded separately. Explicit OS foundry, moulding and western chemical exteriors, including the complete hatched Crown roof body 609; interpreted cuts preserve all seventeen existing height and roof profiles. Four inferred shafts retain their profiles and parent-local offsets within corrected parents. Site 230 tenant identity remains partly unresolved. Replace six unreviewed industrial sketch compounds and the municipal stores yard with complete individually reviewed OS roofs. Heights and gables are estimates; no fire-insurance coverage claimed. Restore independently reviewed enclosed industrial/market roofs east of Channelsea and west of the north–south railway. Exteriors are map/source evidence; every new roof/elevation profile is explicitly interpreted. Open wharf yards, railway sidings and unshaded plant/platform outlines remain context. Replace northern Channelsea–railway sketch blocks with independently reviewed shaded roof exteriors at Brush, Hardware, Langthorn, Varnish/Japan and Abbey works, plus the missing Abbey Road frontage roofs. Every new height and roof form is estimated; no original fire-insurance coverage is asserted. Open courts, moat, railway ground and domestic frontage stay distinct. Bromley gasworks 3 October 2026: OS-led audit of the 1891-96 footprints without models. Long purifier-block sheds, the lodge at B.M. 18.45, the south-west leg of the riverside L-range and small yard and garden buildings added from source outlines; purifier vessel rows refitted to the 44 mapped vessels; scrubber tanks and holders 1-4 moved to circle fits of the mapped column bases. Heights, storeys and roof forms are explicit estimates: the OS gives plan only, no Goad sheet covers the site and no photograph of the works buildings has been found. Retort-house envelopes left for a later pass. Leather Cloth Works 3 October 2026: first models for site 865 (previously excluded as east of Channelsea). 45 of the 50 supplied OS outlines on the site are modelled, merged where they touch; the 3,838 m² northern outline is split into a main shed and its long arm. A hatched street block on the south road (OS lettering "STEPH…") that the GeoPackage omits is traced from the OS mosaic, moved into the GeoPackage frame by the measured (-1.75, +0.25) m offset, and split into three roofs. A small square opening in one range is read as a chimney base. All heights, storeys, roof forms, materials and functions are explicit estimates: the OS gives plan only and no Goad sheet or photograph of this works has been found.

scopeNotes: Includes entire Bromley gasworks production ground as well as nine holders.
Includes Channelsea-side manure works as gasworks northern boundary context.
Includes full East London Soap Works and New Imperial Saw Mills beyond the clipped original GIS edge.
Current-period records are reconstructed from 1893 plans; unproven 1894–1916 additions are not treated as securely dated to 1900.

September 26 street pass: approximate range envelopes are clipped at registered 1893 OS road/pavement corridors. Selected frontage placements corrected after street overlay; original envelope and previous placement retained. Render geometry is still an interpretation, not a measured building survey.

Author-requested western Old Lea industrial frontage from Three Mills to the Great Eastern Main Line, with adjacent Bow industrial ranges. Individual envelopes read from locally archived NLS five-foot OS mapping. Site IDs and uses cross-checked against the supplied Industry_1893-95 dataset. Heights, roofs, chimneys and stock are interpreted for the flyover, not measured reconstructions.
Eastern strip roof exteriors follow the OS plan and supplied footprints; new heights, storeys and roof forms remain explicit estimates without asserted Goad coverage.

buildings.name: Bromley eastern purifier block — west, beside the scrubber enclosure shed
buildings.footprintEvidence: Source outline from the author's 1891–96 OS building GeoPackage (sourceFids 5993), merged across OS internal division lines where listed and simplified at 0.15 m; checked against the cached NLS five-foot 1893 mosaic. Long roofed (shaded) range set between parallel rows of rectangular purifier vessels in the eastern purifier block; OS five-foot plan, London VIII.42, revised 1893; OS internal notches along the long walls (pipe or valve connections) are kept in the outline.
buildings.heightEvidence: Explicit estimate; no measured height, storey mark or photograph of this building at c1900 is available. Single tall storey kept above the c2 m purifier vessels either side; 5.0 m eaves chosen for realism, not evidence.
buildings.roofEvidence: Pitched roof along the range is an interpretation. Sheds serving purifiers were usually ventilated; a ridge ventilator would be appropriate but the renderer has no ventilator option, so a plain gable is proposed. Slate/iron covering not established.
buildings.functionEvidence: Covered shed between purifier rows; probably lime/oxide store or revivifying floor, possibly also housing valves. Function is an interpretation from layout; no label on the OS.
